full_judgment:
8. The P. W. 1, one of the plaintiffs, while deposing in support of plaintiffs' claim of taking settlement of the land in suit stated that at the time of taking pattan Mongal Gazi, Syed Ali, Shahadat, Obaidullah and Hussain Sardar were present but the plaintiffs for the purpose of corroborating P.W. 1 so far his evidence relating to pattan did not examine none of the persons claimed to have been present at the time of pattan but examined P.Ws. 2 and 3 who were not the persons, as mentioned by P.W.1, present at the time of paten. It may also be mentioned no explanation was offered by the plaintiffs for non-examination of the persons who, as being ready for claimed by the P.W.1, were present at the time of pattan. The appellate Court in the afore state of the matter placed no reliance on the P.Ws. 2 and 3 who were examined to corroborate the P.W. 1 as regard the matter of pattan. 

 9. It was the case of the plaintiffs that talk of the pattan took place with the Manager of the Zamindar. In that background the appellate Court observed that no material was brought on record to show that the Manager of the ex- zamindar was competent to settle the land and that no material was also brought on record, that at the time of talk of pattan Zamindar was present or consented to the pattan or received the salami. The appellate Court also noticed that dakhilas produced by the plaintiffs in support of their case of taking pattan of the land in suit do not bear the signature of the Manager who, as claimed by the plaintiffs settled the land, that the scribe of the plaintiffs settled the land, that the scribe of the dakhilas i.e. Naib of the ex-zamindar was not examined and for such non- examination no explanation was offered. On examination and scrutiny of the dakhilas the appellate Court arrived at the finding "The dakhilas Ext.1 series found to have been made old by artificial means and the close scrutiny of the same clearly indicates that the same were written in one sitting by an in-experienced hand  The Ext.1 series in no way inspire confidence about its age as shown thereto", and the claim of the P.Ws.2 and 3 of their being present at the time of pattan can not be accepted since P. W.1 has not stated about the presence of the said witnesses at the time of taking pattan; by the plaintiffs and that the said witnesses "failed to prove the particulars of the dakhilas Ext. 1 series". In the afore state of the matter the appellate Court arrived at the finding "I do not find any reason to believe that they (EWs.2-3) were present at the time of granting the dakhilas Ext. 1 series or their presence at the time of alleged Inman- or that the same i.e. pattan had actually taken place. 

 10. The dakhilas Ext. 1 series filed by the plaintiffs also do not create much confidence. Regard being had to the above facts and circumstances; I am constrained to hold that the story of patan is a mere myth and the dakhilas Ext. 1 series are mere paper transaction and no reliance can be reposed on them. The evidence of possession of the plaintiffs is also found unsatisfactory". Plaintiffs other then P.W.1 examined P.ws. 2 and 3 to prove their claim of possession in the land in suit. The appellate Court on consideration of the evidence of the said witnesses (P.Ws. 2 and 3) arrived at the finding that evidence of record clearly shows that the said P.Ws, do not know the suit land. The appellate Court on consideration of the evidence produced by the plaintiffs in support of their claim of taking pattan of the land in suit has observed" the facts and circumstances so discussed above clearly indicates that the story of pattan of the plaintiffs is not true and the papers (Ext. 1 series) so filed on this behalf are found nothing but forged, collusive, ante-dated and created for the purpose of this suit". The appellate Court has held that the plaintiffs have not acquired title in the land in suit by lapse of time since they had no case in their pleading as regard acquiring title by lapse of time and that no evidence was also led from the plaintiffs' side as regard the case of acquiring title of the land in suit by lapse of time. On the aforesaid findings and decision the appellate Court allowed the appeal and thereupon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissed the suit. 

 16. The appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court has rejected the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3 who examined from the side of the plaintiffs to corroborate the P.W.1 as regard the case of taking pattan of the land from the Ex-zamindar since the said P.Ws. were not the persons whom the P.W.1 stated were present at the time of pattan. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute did not reverse the reasoning and the finding given by the appellate Court in rejecting the evidence of P.Ws. 2 and 3. 

 17. The law is well settled that the extent of jurisdiction of the revisional Court is limited. The revisional Court is within its jurisdiction in reversing the judgment of the lower Court if the same is the result of misreading of the evidence or has been made leaving the legal evidence out of consideration or that while arriving at the decision misconstrued the documentary evidence or left the vital evidence out of consideration without assigning any reason. If the judgment of the lower Court does not suffer from any one of the aforesaid defects the revisional court is not competent to disturb the finding and decision arrived at by the last Court of fact. In the instant case it is seen from the judgment of the appellate Court that the said Court on examination of the documents (Ext. 1 series) arrived at the finding that those are not genuine. The High Court Division did arrived at the finding that the finding so made by the appellate Court was made upon misreading of the evidence or non-consideration of the evidence. The High Court Division without reversing the finding of the appellate Court on the nature and character of the dakhilas (Ext.1 series) exceeded its revisional jurisdiction in disturbing the finding of the appellate Court as regard the genuineness of the dakhilas. Since from the plaintiffs' side no case of misreading or non-consideration of the evidence was made out before the High Court Division as regard the finding arrived at by the appellate Court as to the quality of the Ext.1 series or in other words genuineness of the said Ext. 1 series the said Division erred in re-assessing the evidence as to Ext. 1 series and thereupon disturbing the finding of the last Court of fact as regard the Ext.1 series. It appears the High Court Division based its judgment on certain observations made by the appellate Court as to the infirmity in the case of the defendant and that as to the steps taken by the plaintiffs in proof of its case. The High Court Division while setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court did not at all address itself to the material findings arrived at by the said Court on the question of taking settlement of the land in suit as claimed by the plaintiffs, nature and quality of the dakhilas produced by the plaintiffs in support of their claim of taking settlement of the land in suit, effect of non-examination of the scribe of the dakhilas and that absence of evidence from the side of the plaintiffs as to that Zamindar consented to the pattan and accepted salami and finally finding of the appellate Court as regard possession in the and in suit by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs examining P.W.1 in support of their claim of taking pattan of the land in suit and examined the P.Ws. 2 and 3 for the purpose of corroboration of the evidence of P.W.1 on the point of taking pattan of the land in suit by the plaintiffs. The appellate court upon assigning due reasoning rejected the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3. It may be mentioned the High Court Division has not reversed the finding of the appellate Court relating to discarding the evidence of P.Ws. 2 and 3. The High Court Division overlooked the material fact that there was no reliable evidence to corroborate the evidence of P.W. 1 as regard the material fact of settling the land by the Zamindar to the plaintiffs. The appellate Court discarded the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3 on the question of possession of the land in suit by the plaintiffs. This finding of the appellate Court was also not reversed by the High Court Division while making the Rule absolute. 

 18. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view that the High Court Division was in serious error in disturbing the finding of fact arrived at by the appellate Court when the said Division did not hold that the finding and decision made by the appellate Court was vitiated by non-consideration of the evidence or misreading of evidence or that the appellate Court left the vital evidence out of consideration for no valid reason while making its decision on the question of taking pattan of the land in suit by the plaintiffs and the nature and character of the Ext.1 series as well as regarding possession of the plaintiffs.
